name: Historic Centre of São Luís
description: São Luís, the capital of Maranhão in northern Brazil, sits on an island in the Bay of São Marcos. Its old centre keeps the rectangular street grid laid out in the late 1600s, lined with roughly 4,000 protected buildings from the 18th and 19th centuries. The French founded the town, the Dutch occupied it, and the Portuguese ruled it. An early 20th-century economic slump left many of its fine old buildings standing.
